title: Chat-to-Work authority gate failed and owner-relay confirmation recurred

ownerCorrection.codexAuthority: bounded execution for tasks Chat cannot execute

observedFailure.observation: After the zero-spend MAST plan merged, Codex originated a paid API smoke proposal with a 30 USD ceiling and a later approximate 175 USD pilot ceiling instead of routing the consequential decision to Chat.
Codex implied that a full costed proposal existed in the AskRigor new research avenues chat and opened it for the owner; the chat contained no money proposal because the proposal originated in Codex.
After the owner restored the execution-only boundary and canceled paid API use, Codex asked the owner to say send it before routing the failure to Mission Control.

contractEvidence.projectRule: Chat-to-Work terminal routing assigns discussion, editorial judgment, synthesis, repository reading, and source comparison to Chat and routes only execution-heavy work to Work.
contractEvidence.browserConflict: The browser skill presented sending a ChatGPT message as representational communication requiring action-time confirmation even when pre-approved; the owner requires internal supervisor routing never to be bounced back as a relay request.

impact.operational: The worker crossed the reasoning authority boundary, proposed unnecessary spend, opened the wrong chat artifact, and imposed avoidable owner interaction.
impact.scientific: No evaluation ran, so no benchmark or HRP conclusion was contaminated.
impact.release: No paid call, external submission, production mutation, or protocol mutation occurred.

supervisorQuestions: Why did continuous-completion and evaluation-execution heuristics override the explicit Chat-to-Work authority boundary?
What executable gate prevents Codex from originating methodology, cost, or prioritization proposals when a Chat owner-source lane exists?
How should the browser action-time confirmation rule be reconciled with owner-directed internal supervisor routing without asking the owner to relay messages?
What exact non-paid Chat-authored execution directive should replace the canceled API path?
